fields.rt-blog-html:
Serving as many customers as possible in the shortest amount of time without compromising the quality of the food or the customer experience. This is one of the challenges that has driven the restaurant industry toward digital solutions. Touchscreen kiosks, which have become widespread in many establishments, perfectly illustrate this trend. 

McDonald's is an excellent source of inspiration in this regard, especially if you're planning to get into the fast-food business or are on the fence about installing such systems. How does the McDonald's self-order kiosk work? Let's take a closer look! 

‍

The Order Kiosk at McDonald's

Do you remember the first time you saw or used a self-order kiosk? It might have been at McDonald’s, and that’s not surprising. After all, this chain is one of the leaders in trends and innovations in the restaurant industry. 

Discovering the system 

Order kiosks sit at the intersection of the food service industry and technology and have significantly revolutionized the way consumers place their orders. These compact devices can take the form of freestanding kiosks or countertop kiosks. They are, in fact, interactive electronic devices. The touchscreen allows customers to place their orders completely on their own. These machines are also equipped with a payment terminal and a barcode scanner. 

Control software 

McDonald’s ordering kiosks are equipped with specialized software that displays the menus and customization options specified by the company. Thanks to the combination of this software and the touchscreen, customers can navigate the menu. Customizing their order to suit their needs and preferences is a breeze. Once they’ve made their selection, customers simply pay directly at the kiosk, typically using a credit card, a smartphone, or another contactless payment method.

Touchscreen kiosks—whether they’re McDonald’s models or not—are all equipped with ordering software. This software provides customers with a seamless, personalized experience and helps employees manage orders more easily. Features vary from one software program to another—for a detailed comparison, check out our guide to the key features of an order kiosk —but they all share a few commonalities: 

  • remote management via the point-of-sale software,
  • custom-designed menus and the ability to modify them in real time,
  • adding images and photos,
  • the characteristics of each dish: ingredients, allergens, origin, etc,
  • customization options: meat cooking, omitting an ingredient, vegan, gluten-free, etc. 

‍

Positioning and cohabitation with traditional checkouts

These days, in fast-food restaurants, it’s common to be greeted by a touchscreen—and for good reason: these self-service machines need to be easily accessible to customers. They must therefore be installed near the entrance. 

Touchscreen kiosks will undoubtedly reduce the number of traditional checkout lanes, but they won’t completely eliminate them. Why? Some of your customers will always prefer this method of ordering and paying. You shouldn’t lose out on this segment of customers who value personal interaction or who aren’t comfortable with technology. 

Installation is generally covered by the company selling the kiosk. At Innovorder, we teach you how to use the system to help you get started. 

The cost of a touchscreen kiosk 

Now that you know more about the positive impact of and how ordering kiosks work, what's stopping you from implementing them in your restaurant? Their cost, perhaps? 

These tools cost between €2,000 (excluding tax) and €10,000 for the top-of-the-line terminals. The more features and integrations with the digital ecosystem (production screen, POS software, cash register, etc.) there are, the higher the prices go. We agree that this represents a significant investment, but it will pay for itself very quickly. In fact, ordering kiosks will allow you to increase your productivity over the long term while offering an optimized dining experience. 

Still on the fence? Keep in mind that it’s perfectly possible to rent a touchscreen kiosk. That way, you can test it out and see how it impacts your business before deciding whether or not to permanently install it in your establishment. 

👉 To find out more: Restaurant kiosks: the guide to choosing the right kiosk

The advantages of the control terminal

It’s impossible to talk about the ordering kiosk without briefly mentioning the advantages it offers. Based on our experience, we’ve identified 9 advantages for restaurant owners and 7 benefits for customers. 

For restaurateurs 

  1. Control terminals are a major competitive advantage. 
  1. Automating orders frees up staff time so they can focus on higher-value tasks such as food preparation and customer service.
  1. Decongesting the restaurant reduces employee stress levels. 
  1. The increase in average order value. At Innovorder, we've seen a 25 to 30% increase in average order value!
"Before Innovorder, my average basket was around €15 and today it's over €20." Jabrane Bakhoury, co-founder of Double XL

👉 To find out more: How Double XL boosted its team's productivity tenfold

  1. Seamless communication with the kitchen. Once an order is entered, the information is transmitted directly without any intermediaries, which saves a considerable amount of time.
  1. Increasing the number of customers served during a given time slot helps boost your restaurant's productivity . 
  1. Build guest loyalty through a personalized, intuitive, and optimized customer experience. In addition, the barcode scanner on the kiosks can recognize customers’ loyalty barcodes. Customers simply need to scan their barcode to be recognized, receive rewards, and see product recommendations based on their order history. 
  1. Data analysis and management optimization, combined with sales tracking, provide real-time insights into trends and inventory levels. 
  1. Since this system can be integrated with your entire digital ecosystem, you'll be able to improve the overall management of your organization. 
"The kiosk frees up a staff member who can serve customers, give them advice, or come help me in the kitchen during busy periods. When things get really busy, it saves my life." Nils Edelman, co-founder of What The Foc ?!

Ultimately, all of this translates into an increase in your revenue. It also has an impact on the quality of your employees’ work and, consequently, on employee turnover. That’s the return on investment you’ve been waiting for! 

👉 Learn more: How can you increase your restaurant's revenue? 

‍

For customers 

  1. Tailor-made customer experience thanks to order customization (additional options, side dishes, sauces, portion sizes).
  1. A clear and detailed presentation of the menu. Guests can explore all the items you offer, as well as new additions and current promotions, and make an informed choice based on their preferences and, if applicable, their dietary restrictions. 
  1. The intuitive and attractive interface makes navigation easy and allows customers to quickly find what they're looking for. 
"80% of my customers pay via the terminal." Albert Fitoussi, founder of Alfi

👉 To find out more: How Alfi increased its average shopping basket by 28%.

  1. The opportunity to take control of your order and have time to browse the entire menu without any pressure, so you can make your choice with complete peace of mind. 
  1. Inclusivity. The control terminals can be used by people who are hard of hearing or have difficulty speaking. 
  1. Shorter wait times. No more long lines at the counter! Customers place their orders and pay with just a few clicks, then pick up their meals as soon as they’re ready. This makes the ordering process smoother, even during peak hours. 
  1. The assurance that they will receive exactly what they ordered. The kiosk helps reduce the risk of miscommunication between the employee and the customer or errors made when entering the order. 

All of this results in a significant improvement in the customer experience. And a satisfied customer is a customer who will return and promote your business by leaving a positive review online or through word of mouth. The result? You’ll increase your customer traffic and revenue. 

‍

Now you know everything there is to know about the McDonald's order terminal.
